observations: Photo 0: a white game console with a flat three-layer slab body, the shape of a PS4 Pro, lying on cardboard boxes in a shop.
Photo 0: no brand logo, model name or label is readable on the console; the top is partly covered by boxes and cables.
Photo 0: two sealed retail boxes marked 'Wireless Controller' and 'X6', with small print naming several platforms; these are boxed generic third-party pads, not Sony DualShock 4 pads.
Photo 0: a power cord with a UK three-pin plug and a black HDMI-type cable.
Photo 0: no receipt, no screen, no powered-on view, no ports or rear panel shown.
Photo 0 carries a dealer watermark; there is only one photo and nothing ties it to a specific unit.

identity.kind: PS4 Pro game console (white), identified by its three-layer body shape

claims.evidence: Photo 0 body shape matches a PS4 Pro but no logo, label or system screen is readable.
The visible top and front look clean in photo 0, but sides, rear and ports are not shown.
No photo of the rear warranty seal or case screws.
Needs a long running clip at minimum; cannot be judged from a still.
No ports shown and no clip of HDMI picture or USB charging.
Photo 0 shows two boxed generic 'Wireless Controller' X6 pads, not original Sony DualShock 4 pads.
No receipt appears in the photo.

risks.risk: Console may not power on, may not read discs, or may have a failed HDMI port or hard drive.
risks.proof: Clip powering it on to the home screen on a TV, playing a game, with the HDMI cable in shot.

risks.risk: It may not be a PS4 Pro or may have a smaller or swapped hard drive.
risks.proof: Screenshot of Settings > System > System Information showing model CUH-7xxx and storage.
risks.if_unproven: as a PS4 Pro console only, untested

risks.risk: Overheating or loud fan from dust or dried thermal paste.
risks.proof: Clip of 15 minutes of gameplay with the fan audible and the console in shot.

risks.risk: Opened or repaired before, or jailbroken or console-banned from the network.
risks.proof: Close photo of the rear seal and screws plus a screenshot of the console signed in to PlayStation Network.

risks.risk: The photo may be a dealer stock shot, not the unit for sale.
risks.proof: Photo of the console with a handwritten note carrying today's date and a code we give, plus the serial label on the back.
risks.if_unproven: as unconfirmed unit, held at worst case

proof_requests: Clip powering on to the home screen and running a game, with a handwritten dated code in shot.
Screenshot of System Information showing the CUH model number and storage.
Photo of the rear panel showing serial label, ports and the warranty seal.
Photo of the pads actually included; if original DualShock 4 pads are claimed, show them.
response.reason: The three-layer body makes it a PS4 Pro by shape, so it can be priced at worst case as an untested console with generic third-party pads. The 'original pads' claim is contradicted by the photo and the receipt, ports and overheating claims are unproven.
